summary: Create a small `board` capability. The board rules survive the deletion test: removing it would push filtering, grouping, cross-capability joining, and label-visibility enforcement into the route or work-items. Direct page composition would make `app/**` own business/security policy; letting work-items call labels would couple independently changeable capabilities. Keep the RSC page thin and place orchestration in board application code.

tree.purpose: RSC entry point. Calls the board RSC surface and renders route-private presentation.
Route-private, server-rendered board presentation. Receives only the safe board projection.
Framework-neutral operation: removes archived items, resolves referenced labels, rejects inaccessible labels, attaches label details, and groups items by status.
Board-owned capability-shaped ports such as `loadWorkItems(actorScope)` and `resolveLabels(actorScope, ids)`.
Board projection and typed expected outcomes; contains no persistence rows or framework types.
Implements the board work-items port using `src/modules/work-items/server.ts` only.
Implements the board labels port using `src/modules/labels/server.ts` only; translates their public contract into board port values.
Server-only public surface for the RSC consumer. Obtains trusted request identity, wires adapters, invokes `loadBoard`, and maps outcomes to RSC behavior.
Existing narrow trusted server API owned by work-items; retains work-item authorization and persistence ownership.
Existing narrow trusted server API owned by labels; returns visible details plus a non-disclosing denied result for requested IDs.
Unit tests board policy using port fakes.
Tests authentication, outcome mapping, redacted reporting, and report-once behavior.
RSC integration test proving the page renders the safe grouped projection through public surfaces.

flows: `src/app/board/page.tsx` → `src/modules/board/rsc.ts` → authenticate current request and construct actor/tenant/request context → `application/load-board.ts`.
`load-board` → board work-items port → `server/work-items-adapter.ts` → `work-items/server.ts` → private work-items store, which applies tenant/ownership predicates.

After filtering archived items, `load-board` collects referenced label IDs → board labels port → `server/labels-adapter.ts` → `labels/server.ts` → private labels store, which applies tenant/visibility predicates. This call is sequential because its IDs come from the filtered work items.

The operation rejects the load with a generic typed authorization outcome if any referenced label is denied; otherwise it attaches returned label details, groups items by status, and returns a board-owned projection.
`board/rsc.ts` maps the authorization outcome to the product’s access-denied RSC behavior and returns successful data to `page.tsx`; provider outages and defects remain exceptions.

decisions.choice: Board owns orchestration and projection policy
decisions.rationale: These rules have independent product meaning and cannot belong to either source capability without coupling or misplaced ownership.

decisions.choice: `app → board`; board server adapters → work-items and labels public server surfaces
decisions.rationale: Work-items and labels never import one another or board. Board application code depends only on its own ports, keeping the graph acyclic.
The only stated consumer is an RSC page. No board `server.ts`, action, client, HTTP, or reusable UI surface is justified.

decisions.choice: Authenticate at `board/rsc.ts`; enforce board policy in `load-board`; retain source authorization and store predicates in each owning capability
decisions.rationale: Identity comes from the request, never page parameters. Defense remains present at channel, business-policy, and persistence boundaries.

decisions.choice: Reject the entire board projection with a generic denied outcome
decisions.rationale: Silently dropping labels would produce misleading data; exposing which label failed could leak its existence.

decisions.choice: Report unexpected exceptions once at `board/rsc.ts`; do not report inside the pure operation or adapters
decisions.rationale: Expected access denial is a typed outcome. Outages and defects carry request/trace context but redact actor, item, label, and provider details.

decisions.choice: Test observable policy and boundary behavior
decisions.rationale: Cover archived-item removal, grouping, label deduplication/attachment, denied-label rejection, empty states, source failures, tenant isolation, redaction, and exactly-once reporting without asserting incidental adapter call counts.

risks: The existing work-items or labels server surfaces may be too broad or may leak persistence rows. Narrow them in their owning modules to board-required values rather than importing internals.
If labels cannot distinguish missing from inaccessible records safely, define a single non-disclosing unresolved/denied contract and map both to the same board denial.
A production build and import-boundary tests should ensure `rsc.ts` and source `server.ts` surfaces are marked `server-only` and cannot enter client bundles.
